acceptance: One durable write-then-rename implementation in go/internal/atomicwrite, with its fault branches tested
storage.writeJSONAtomic, seal.writeSegment and ledgerartifacts.writeAtomically delegate to it with unchanged behaviour (their existing tests stay green)
seal.writeSegment also fsyncs its directory after the rename
fix: Add one durable variant to atomicwrite: a mode argument, file fsync before close, and directory fsync after rename. Move the three writers onto it, keeping each caller's mode and error wording, and keep atomicwrite's fault seams covering the new branches.
source: console, carry F5 fix round (engineering-craft audit: search-before-write found the third durable writer)
summary: atomicwrite.Bytes is the repo's single crash-safe writer, but it never fsyncs. So three packages carry their own durable copy of temp-write, fsync, rename: storage.writeJSONAtomic (state.json, named as an exception in atomicwrite's doc), ledger seal.writeSegment (fsyncs the file, not the directory) and ledgerartifacts.writeAtomically (fsyncs the file and the fan-out directory, mode 0444, added 2026-10-06 for ADR-0123 D2). That is the rule-of-three point.
title: Three durable write-then-rename writers exist; atomicwrite should own the durable variant
